description: Cooldown, not tip-chasing. SECURITY.md explains the trade: staying at the tip of every dependency shortens the distance to a future security fix, but puts this repo in the first wave to install any newly published release — exactly the population a compromised-maintainer attack targets. Neither `cargo audit` nor `pnpm audit` defends against that, because a freshly malicious release has no advisory yet by construction. `minimumReleaseAge` is what does: malicious versions are typically yanked within hours, so a release that has survived a week unremarked is a different risk to one published an hour ago.
js/.npmrc carries the same floor for manual `pnpm update`/`pnpm add`, which Renovate never sees.

packageRules.description: `bump` raises the manifest floor, not just the lock, so the caret keeps telling the truth about what we build against. The default `replace` never moves a floor that a new release already satisfies — which is how these went stale.
Batched into one PR: individually they are noise, together one CI run a week.
One PR each — these usually need a code change (reqwest 0.12 -> 0.13, tokio-tungstenite 0.24 -> 0.29 both did), so they must not ride in a batch.
Native-toolchain adapters (Aeron needs clang + cmake >= 3.30; zmq/rdkafka build C). Slow CI legs — keep them out of the batch so they fail alone.
pyo3 drives the abi3 wheel contract that collapses the publish matrix to one job per platform. Needs the wheel build checked; never automerge.
Our own crates move in lockstep via bump.yml (cargo set-version).

Keep the SHA pins pinned. Actions are pinned to a commit SHA with a `# vX` trailer (see SECURITY.md "Pinning GitHub Actions"); pinDigests makes Renovate maintain both halves rather than proposing a move back to a floating tag.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A cooldown is a defence against releases with no advisory yet. It must never delay a fix for one that is already public — those go out at any time, at any age.
